qt: to the Commission Nikolaos Anadiotis (NI) Subject:

The European Commission is aiming to triple the capacity of data centres in the EU within the next five to seven years. On 21 September 2026, it proposed a common rating scheme for their performance based on energy and water usage, acknowledging that the development of data centres puts extra pressure on power grids and water resources1. In Greece, the rapid concentration of data centres in Attica is already generating significant energy needs. According to recent information, more than 500 MW have been set aside for this infrastructure, limiting network headroom and requiring new lines and substations2. Greece’s electricity network operator ADMIE now publishes specific information concerning data centre connection requests3. The Commission emphasises that network charges must reflect the costs of respective user groups and that the digital sector has a responsibility to ensure the sustainable integration of data centres into the energy system4. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
How will it ensure that the cost of boosting networks to meet the needs of data centres will not be disproportionately passed on to households and SMEs?
Will it establish principles for data centres to bear the network investment costs directly linked to their operation?
Will it include criteria for additional net generation, flexibility and water usage in resource-constrained areas in its upcoming efficiency standards?
